Generate Initial Seurat Clustering for SoupX Estimation

Source: R/Pre-processing_soupX.R
create_seurat_for_clustering.Rd

Batch processes a list of filtered count matrices through a rapid, standard Seurat pipeline (LogNormalization, Variable Feature selection, Scaling, PCA, Neighborhood Graph construction, Clustering, and UMAP). The primary purpose of this function is to quickly generate the high-resolution clusters (defaulting to resolution = 1.8) required by SoupX. Over-clustering at this stage is highly recommended for accurate ambient RNA profiling via SoupX::autoEstCont().

Usage

create_seurat_for_clustering(cts_filtered_list, sample_names)

Arguments

cts_filtered_list

A named list of filtered sparse count matrices, typically generated by the filtered element of load_counts().

sample_names

Character vector. A list of sample identifiers used as keys to match the matrices in the list and assign project names to the Seurat objects.

Value

A named list of processed Seurat objects. Each object contains a standard PCA, UMAP embedding, and high-resolution cluster identities stored in the active Idents.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Assuming you have already loaded your filtered matrices
counts_list <- load_counts(my_samples, "data/filtered", "data/raw")

# Quickly cluster all samples to prepare them for SoupX
initial_seurat_list <- create_seurat_for_clustering(
  cts_filtered_list = counts_list$filtered,
  sample_names = my_samples
)

# The clusters from these objects can now be extracted and fed into SoupChannels
# e.g., soup_channels[[1]] <- setClusters(soup_channels[[1]],
# initial_seurat_list[[1]]$seurat_clusters)
} # }
